contracts.commit_point: Immediately before tool execution: the before_tool_callback invocation on mcp_kb_agent, prior to dispatch of the MCP request leaving the org boundary (agent.py L224-L226 comment: 'this query also leaves the org's boundary (to the MCP server), so it gets the same guardrail').
contracts.declared_mechanism: ADK before_tool_callback: async validate_tool_params (tools.py L24-L87) serializes the entire args dict to a lowercase string, substring-matches it against six sensitive keywords, and returns {'error': ...} to block the call (L76-L86) or None to allow (L87); wired onto mcp_kb_agent via before_tool_callback=validate_tool_params (agent.py L237).
contracts.forbidden_condition: An MCP toolset execution whose arguments dict, serialized via str(args).lower(), contains any substring from the sensitive-keyword list (private_key, aws_key, gcp_key, token, client_secret, password) — i.e., developer secrets or credentials embedded in the outbound query parameters.
pending_binding_information: ADK framework source is not supplied, so the blocking semantics of a non-None dict return from before_tool_callback for MCP toolset calls rest on docstrings/comments rather than framework code.
The set of MCP tools resolved at runtime by AgentRegistry.get_mcp_toolset is not enumerated in supplied source.
Concrete transport of the call to the MCP server is absent from supplied source; the http stratum is inferred from the comment that the query leaves the org's boundary to the MCP server.
contracts.protected_operation: Model-initiated execution of the developer_kb_mcp toolset functions on mcp_kb_agent (query of internal developer documentation built from {triage_summary}).
contracts.protected_resource: The outbound request to the external Developer KB MCP server (projects/{PROJECT_ID}/locations/{MCP_SERVER_LOCATION}/mcpServers/{MCP_SERVER_NAME}) carrying the tool-call arguments/query text.
contracts.protection_obligation: Block any Developer-KB MCP toolset call issued by mcp_kb_agent whose serialized arguments contain sensitive credential keywords (private_key, aws_key, gcp_key, token, client_secret, password), enforced by the validate_tool_params before_tool_callback at the pre-execution commit point — the last checkpoint before the query leaves the org boundary to the MCP server.
scope_limits: Same acknowledged best-effort limitation: the coordinator's triage_summary rewrite and mcp_kb_agent's own reformulation can drop a trigger keyword before the callback sees it (tools.py L44-L54; agent.py L226 'and the same limitation applies').

The guard covers all functions exposed by the developer_kb_mcp toolset as invoked by mcp_kb_agent; the concrete exposed tool names are resolved at runtime via registry.get_mcp_toolset and are not enumerated in source (agent.py L212-L222).
Detection is a lowercase substring match against only six listed keywords (tools.py L64-L76); other secret formats are missed and benign text containing e.g. 'token' can trigger false positives.

Registered only on mcp_kb_agent and web_search_agent; internal agents (search_vais_agent, internal_analyst) and the deterministic query_bq node carry no such callback (agent.py L126-L129; tools.py L35-L37).

contracts.protected_operation: Model-initiated execution of the GoogleSearchTool on web_search_agent (search of public developer sources built from {triage_summary}).
contracts.protected_resource: The outbound external Google Search request carrying the tool-call arguments/query text (data leaving the org boundary).
contracts.protection_obligation: Block any GoogleSearchTool call issued by web_search_agent whose serialized arguments contain sensitive credential keywords (private_key, aws_key, gcp_key, token, client_secret, password), enforced by the validate_tool_params before_tool_callback at the pre-execution commit point — the last checkpoint before the query text leaves the org boundary via the external search call.
scope_limits: Best-effort net only: the callback sees only the arguments generated for the current tool call, not the raw user input; the coordinator's triage_summary rewrite and web_search_agent's own reformulation can legitimately drop a trigger keyword, so a secret in the original report is not guaranteed to be caught (agent.py L184-L194; tools.py L44-L54).
Detection is a lowercase substring match against only six listed keywords (tools.py L64-L76); other secret formats are missed and benign text containing e.g. 'token' can trigger false positives.

Registered only on the two external-facing agents (web_search_agent, mcp_kb_agent); search_vais_agent is deliberately unguarded because its Vertex AI Search queries never leave the org datastore (agent.py L126-L129; tools.py L35-L37).
The guard is per-agent wiring, not an app-level or workflow-level policy; it does not inspect other lifecycle stages such as LLM requests or synthesis output.
